arguments.value: 31-year-old pregnant woman at 24 weeks gestation presented with fever, gastrointestinal illness, severe hypokalaemia with normal anion gap metabolic acidosis, and progressive quadriparesis progressing to altered sensorium requiring intubation. Workup suggested distal renal tubular acidosis from previously unrecognized Sjögren’s syndrome (SSA/RO-52 positive, dry mouth/eye symptoms, positive Schirmer’s test), with concurrent IgM leptospira infection. She improved after aggressive potassium and bicarbonate replacement, ventilation, and treatment of the underlying infections/autoimmune condition, and later delivered a healthy infant at term.
